page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-80 is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual machine featuring 80 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 40 Intel physical cores with two threads per core. The instance is provisioned with 160 GB of system memory, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. It incorporates 260 MB of shared L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1 data cache per core. Advanced instruction set support includes AVX-512 vector extensions and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX tile and int8) for accelerated matrix operations, alongside AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic instructions. Local storage is not bundled, requiring persistent network-attached block storage for persistent data requirements, and no GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong multi-threaded compute and data-processing capabilities. The server achieves a stress-ng multi-core score of 68334.5 and a PassMark CPU score of 71998.05, placing it in the top 25 percent of tested machines, while single-core performance remains average. Memory subsystem performance shows a large-block uncached read bandwidth of 286.55 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 123.86 GB/sec. The machine records top-tier results in static web serving throughput at 102.77 GB/sec and image processing workloads. Highly parallel tasks such as software compilation with Clang and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression also evaluate in the top quartile.

From an architectural standpoint, the 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation prioritizes parallel CPU throughput over per-thread memory capacity. The integrated AMX instructions enable CPU-based machine learning inference, delivering 261.35 tokens per second for prompt processing on medium 7B models without requiring dedicated accelerator hardware. The primary trade-off rests in the absence of onboard NVMe storage and the lower RAM ratio, meaning memory-heavy in-memory databases may encounter capacity limits.

The n4-highcpu-80 is best suited for compute-intensive enterprise workloads, including large-scale software compilation, distributed CI/CD build pipelines, batch media processing, CPU-based machine learning inference, and high-concurrency web serving tiers.
